Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.6.2 until 6.7, PATCH /api/config accepts unfiltered CivetWeb lua_* options through webserver.advancedOpts, while POST /api/teleporter writes attacker-controlled content from a dhcp.leases archive entry through src/zip/teleporter.c without content validation. An authenticated administrator can place controlled file content on disk, point a Lua execution option at that file, and rely on the advancedOpts configuration change to restart FTL. CivetWeb then executes the file as Lua through the processing in src/webserver/webserver.c, allowing arbitrary commands to run as the pihole operating-system user and persist across restarts while the configuration and file remain. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. Prior to 6.7, log_http_access in src/webserver/webserver.c writes attacker-controlled User-Agent content to the access log without output neutralization when debug.api is enabled. If an administrator configures files.log.webserver inside webserver.paths.webroot with a filename matching lua_server_page_pattern, an unauthenticated request can plant Lua markup in that log and a later request can cause CivetWeb to evaluate the log as a Lua server page. The resulting commands run as the pihole operating-system user and can access or modify pihole-owned configuration, credentials, databases, logs, and rendered interface content. When the log is not served through the Lua handler, the same unneutralized writer still permits log forgery and downstream log-parser injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, validation in src/api/list.c permits spaces for GRAVITY_GROUPS and consequently skips carriage-return and line-feed validation for group names submitted through POST /api/groups. The unsanitized name is copied into the Location value in pi_hole_extra_headers, and CivetWeb interprets embedded CR/LF sequences as separate HTTP response headers. An authenticated administrator can therefore inject headers such as Set-Cookie, Location, or Cache-Control; when a browser processes the response, this can cause session fixation, attacker-controlled redirects, or cache behavior changes. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

Ikaros is a content management system for ACGMN media. Prior to 1.2.0, server/src/main/java/run/ikaros/server/core/tag/TagEndpoint.java does not enforce tag ownership for authenticated users with tag permissions. GET /tags/condition accepts an arbitrary userId and can enumerate another user's tags, DELETE /tag/id/{id} deletes a tag without comparing its owner to the requester, and DELETE /tag/condition omits userId from its filter and can delete every user's tags matching the supplied condition. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.0.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, an authenticated Agent with folder write access can use POST /upload to store HTML or SVG content that GET /download/{path} serves from the application origin through server/src/handlers/download.rs. The response sets Content-Disposition: inline and lacks forced attachment handling and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, allowing the browser to render the uploaded active content as the application. When a victim opens the link, the script can access the JavaScript-readable atomic_session cookie and the Agent private key in same-origin IndexedDB, enabling persistent account impersonation. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, the Commit application path in lib/src/commit.rs allows an authenticated Agent to assign the server-managed internalId property to an owned resource without character validation. The /download handler in server/src/handlers/download.rs passes that value to filesystem path construction and NamedFile::open without sanitization, containment validation, or a File-class check, so traversal or absolute paths can read files available to the server process. Reading the server configuration can expose the root Agent private key and allow root impersonation with full read, write, and delete access to server data. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.29.0 to 0.40.2, Atomic Server provisions a well-known /setup invite with write enabled, the Drive root as its target, and usagesLeft set to one. construct_invite_redirect in server/src/plugins/invite.rs discards the redeemer identity, so an unauthenticated request containing an attacker-controlled public-key can create a new Agent and grant it write access to the entire Drive. On a fresh, unclaimed deployment, this permits reading, modifying, or deleting resources, changing permissions, and creating or altering Agents. No complete fixed version was verified as of this review.

Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. Prior to 0.40.3, unauthenticated requests to /bookmark can supply a url that server/src/plugins/bookmark.rs passes through fetch_data to fetch_body. Endpoint dispatch in lib/src/db.rs invokes the handler before check_read, and lib/src/client/helpers.rs previously checked only that the URL began with HTTP, without restricting loopback, private, link-local, DNS-rebinding, or redirect targets. The handler reflects fetched content in returned resource fields, making this a full-response server-side request forgery that can expose internal services and plain-GET cloud metadata. The short request timeout limits slow targets, and metadata services requiring a separate token request are outside the demonstrated GET-only path. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, check_client_auth() in src/api/auth.c detects that a matching session identifier has passed valid_until but still assigns user_id before the expired state can be rejected. That assignment sends execution through the authorized branch, renews valid_until for another timeout interval, and leaves the session-expired response unreachable. An attacker who possesses a previously valid session identifier can periodically reuse it to preserve administrative access indefinitely, making the configured session timeout ineffective. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Financial Management product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Security). The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Financial Management. Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Hyperion Financial Management accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.2 (Confidentiality impacts). CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N).

desc: Instatic is an open source visual content management system for building static websites. Prior to 0.0.14, isSafeUrl() and safeUrl() in src/core/html-sanitize/index.ts remove tabs, newlines, carriage returns, and characters handled by String.prototype.trim(), but leave other leading C0 control characters that browsers discard before parsing a URL scheme. A low-privileged editor can place a dangerous URL behind one of those controls in a URL property or custom HTML attribute, allowing src/core/publisher/escapeProps.ts and the shared URL sanitizer to emit it into rendered content. When an Owner or Admin activates the element in the same-origin admin editor canvas, script executes with the victim's application authority and can drive admin APIs to read protected data, create an owner account, or install a plugin. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.14.

OmniFaces is a utility library for Faces. From 5.2 until 5.4.3, applications using <o:sse> or @Push(type=SSE) with session scope, view scope, or a user attribute can expose pushed messages because org.omnifaces.cdi.push.SseEndpoint#doGet accepts a channel identifier registered by SseChannelManager and PushSessionManager without verifying that the caller's HTTP session owns it. An attacker who obtains the victim's channel identifier from a logged URL, report, Referer header, or shared link can connect from a foreign or absent session and receive messages intended for the victim. Application-scoped channels are intentionally unbound, and this issue permits message receipt but not message injection. This issue is fixed in version 5.4.3.

desc: Typecho before 1.3.1-rc contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the XML-RPC pingback.ping method where checkSafeHost() validates a hostname's resolved IP once but the subsequent outbound request performs an independent DNS resolution, creating a TOCTOU window exploitable via DNS rebinding. An unauthenticated attacker can configure a domain to return a benign IP at validation time and an internal address (loopback, RFC1918, or cloud metadata IP) at request time, causing the server to issue blind SSRF requests to arbitrary internal hosts and ports.

desc: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J of Apache log4net. Both layouts split a message holding the CDATA end marker into several CDATA sections, but searched for the marker with a culture-sensitive comparison. Ignorable characters or a combining mark around the marker made the search miss it, so the CDATA section stayed open. From 3.3.1 on, an XML parser then reads the following log events as part of that message; earlier versions leave the log file not well-formed. A party whose data reaches a log message could hide later log events from a consumer that parses the XML log. This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform. From 4.3-milestone-1 until 16.10.18, 17.10.5, and 18.2.0, the /rest/wikis/{wikiName}/query REST endpoint permits HQL query construction that can combine blind conditions with FROM-clause injection to join BaseObject and StringProperty, bypassing the SELECT-column whitelist. An unauthenticated attacker can recover database values from inaccessible pages, including salted SHA1 password hashes and passwords stored in configuration properties. It should be assumed that, with more complex techniques, this can work even when the attacker cannot read any wiki page. A typical password hash may require roughly 800 requests, and expensive injected queries can also degrade availability. The issue is remediated by disabling HQL and XWQL REST queries by default. This issue is fixed in versions 16.10.18, 17.10.5, and 18.2.0.

Servo is a lightweight, high-performance web rendering engine for embedding web technologies in applications. Prior to 0.3.0, a sandboxed iframe can use declarative refresh to auto-navigate because RefreshRedirectDue::invoke() in components/script/dom/document/document.rs does not enforce the sandboxed automatic-features flag. The bypass occurs with sandbox="", sandbox="allow-same-origin", sandbox="allow-forms", and sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-forms". Attacker-controlled framed content can replace itself without user action, enabling framed phishing, content replacement, redirect loops, and limited denial of service, but the issue does not by itself permit script execution or parent DOM access. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.0.

desc: Servo is a lightweight, high-performance web rendering engine for embedding web technologies in applications. Prior to 0.4.0, a frame with sandbox="" can reach and execute a javascript: URL through declarative refresh because RefreshRedirectDue::invoke() in components/script/dom/document/document.rs can reach JavaScript URL handling in components/script/script_thread.rs without enforcing the sandbox's script prohibition. This gives attacker-controlled content arbitrary JavaScript execution in a frame intended to be scriptless, including nested DOM probe creation and blind browser requests. The frame retains an opaque origin, so the issue does not by itself provide parent DOM access. This issue is fixed in version 0.4.0.

October System provides the system module for October Content Management System. Prior to 3.7.18 and 4.3.2, the Media Library MediaManager::onCropImage and cropImage path accepts a user-controlled destination filename without applying the default_extensions allowlist enforced by the normal upload path. An authenticated backend user with media.library.create permission can upload arbitrary bytes under an allowed extension and use the zero-dimension crop branch, which performs a byte-for-byte File::copy, to write those bytes into the public media folder under an attacker-selected extension. Default server configurations block PHP execution in that folder, but HTML or SVG output can produce stored cross-site scripting in the application origin; non-default servers that execute PHP in the media directory can expose remote code execution. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.7.18 and 4.3.2.

desc: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, web/controle/control.php authorizes FuncionarioControle requests only by checking whether an authenticated employee has a permission row for resource 11 or 91, while MiddlewareDAO::verificarPermissao() does not compare the stored id_acao value or authorize the requested method. An employee with any such permission and a valid CSRF token from the employee's own session can invoke FuncionarioControle::adicionarPermissao, FuncionarioControle::alterarPermissao, or FuncionarioControle::excluirPermissao to add, change, or remove permissions for arbitrary roles. This can grant higher action levels over sensitive resources, expose or modify protected employee, patient, configuration, and administrative data, or disrupt legitimate access by changing other roles. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.

desc: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, a user with backup-management permission can upload a crafted gzip-compressed tar archive through web/html/configuracao/importar_dump.php, after which web/controle/control.php accepts a user-controlled modulo value and combines it with nomeClasse for require_once(). By using a phar:// path to the uploaded archive and selecting the whitelisted InternoControle, whose empty resource list is treated as authorized, the user can cause an embedded controller file and its requested method to execute as the web-server process. The attack path depends on the configured BKP_DIR, and enabling phar.readonly or phar.require_hash does not prevent PHP from reading the gzip tar archive through phar://. Successful exploitation permits access to or modification of sensitive data, configuration, credentials, source files, host commands, and services reachable by the web-server account. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.

Converting crafted CP949 input to UTF-8 character encoding and ignoring invalid characters, in the GNU C Library version 2.1 or later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash. When the CP949 decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\xa2\xe8' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice. If //IGNORE is set on the destination encoding and this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer. To exploit this, the target iconv function needs to set //IGNORE on the destination of the conversion and the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Converting crafted ISO-2022-CN-EXT input in the GNU C Library version 2.2 through 2.44 may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash. When the ISO-2022-CN-EXT decoder encounters an invalid input byte sequence like '\x0e' it ends up advancing the pointer tracking the read buffer position twice. If this sequence is at the end of the input buffer, the decoder may then end up reading past the bounds of the input buffer. To exploit this, the input and encoding needs to be attacker controlled.

desc: Converting crafted input from UCS-4 to IBM1390 or IBM1399 character encoding, in the GNU C Library version 2.3.3 and later may result in the converter reading past the end of the input buffer, causing the calling application to crash. When converting from UCS-4, these encoders may encounter a combining base such as U+00E6 and jump ahead by 4 bytes to check the next UCS-4 code point. The check for end of buffer however does not account for this, which may result in a buffer overread if the following code point has less than 4 bytes remaining. Exploitation of this bug not only requires attacker control of input and encoding, but also strict control over layout of the input in memory.

Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the FileAppender, RollingFileAppender, UdpAppender and SmtpAppender of Apache log4net. Characters the configured encoding could not represent were converted by that encoding's best-fit fallback, which turns fullwidth characters such as U+FF1C, U+FF1E and U+FF02 into <, > and ". The conversion happened after XmlLayout or XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J had escaped the text, so a party whose data reaches a log message could forge complete log events in an XML log, for example a fake audit entry. On .NET Framework this needs no configuration where the ANSI code page is single-byte, since that is the default encoding; on .NET it needs a configured single-byte encoding such as ISO-8859-1. This is the best-fit conversion described by the WorstFit research. This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

desc: Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character vulnerability in the AdoNetAppender of Apache log4net. Text parameters were bound unchanged, so a NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate reached the database as it was. A database that refuses such a value, such as PostgreSQL, rejected the insert and the event was lost; only the first such loss per appender was reported. A party whose data reaches a log message could suppress that event. This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

desc: IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because update_self_from_url fetches it over cleartext HTTP with no integrity check. Called with no argument, as the module's documentation shows, the updater fetches the list from the `http://` address in the URL constant and checks only that the request succeeded, with no signature or digest over the response. The lines that come back are written into the module's own source file as the built-in list. An attacker on the network path when the updater runs chooses the suffix boundary the module reports to every caller on the host, and that answer persists in the installed module until it is reinstalled. Dropping one rule makes the hostname check in IO::Socket::SSL accept a wildcard certificate that spans the whole public suffix that rule named.

IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source. The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl. Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.

Poppler pdfdetach 24.03.0 through 26.11.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in utils/pdfdetach.cc that allows attackers to write files outside the output directory by bypassing a string-prefix containment check. Attackers can craft PDFs with embedded file names containing '..' sequences or absolute paths, so -saveall or -savefile extraction creates or overwrites files with the invoking user's privileges.

Poppler pdftohtml through 26.11.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in HtmlLink::getLinkStart() in utils/HtmlLinks.cc that writes PDF link annotation URIs into href attributes without escaping in HTML output modes. Attackers can craft a PDF whose /URI entry contains a double quote followed by HTML markup or event handlers to execute script in browsers viewing the generated HTML.

Poppler through 26.11.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in the libcurl-based remote file loader that trusts unvalidated HEAD Content-Length values in CurlCachedFileLoader::init(). Malicious HTTP servers can return an enormous Content-Length so CachedFile resizes its chunk cache accordingly, aborting pdfinfo or PDFDocFactory-based applications with std::bad_alloc for denial of service.

desc: Poppler 21.01.0 through 26.11.0 contains a time-of-check time-of-use race condition in FormWidgetSignature::signDocument() that allows local attackers to obtain valid signatures over altered content. Attackers with write access to the output file or directory can overwrite or swap the PDF between writing and hashing, causing the signer's key to sign attacker-controlled content.

Poppler 0.76.1 through 26.11.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SplashOutputDev::iccTransform() that allows attackers to write out of bounds when rendering in splashModeDeviceN8. Attackers can supply a PDF with an ICCBased image whose alternate is DeviceN, causing getDeviceNLine() to overflow the per-row buffer, crashing the renderer and corrupting heap memory.

Poppler through 26.11.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in NSSCryptoSignBackend.cc that allows attackers to trigger reads of freed CMS arena memory during repeated signature verification. Attackers can supply a signed PDF embedding the signer certificate to crash applications or pdfsig runs validating multiple signatures, or cause incorrect certificate validation results.

Snap7 through 1.4.3 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in TSnap7MicroClient::opReadMultiVars() that allows malicious PLCs to overflow client buffers via unchecked DataLength fields. Attackers controlling or impersonating a PLC can return crafted ReadVar responses to Cli_ReadMultiVars() callers, writing up to 65535 bytes per item to corrupt memory and crash clients.

desc: ILIAS 11.0 before 11.6 contains an sql injection vulnerability in RegistrationCodeRepository::getCodesData() that concatenates unvalidated sort fields into an ORDER BY clause. Authenticated users with read access to the Authentication and Registration administration node can supply SQL expressions as the sort parameter to extract database contents via boolean-based inference.

ILIAS before 9.25, 10.13, and 11.6 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in ilPRGAssignmentFilter::toConditions() that allows authenticated users to inject SQL through the StudyProgramme members list Name and Status filters. Attackers holding only the OrgUnit permission to view members can break out of LIKE literals and execute stacked statements, such as overwriting the root password hash to gain administrative control.

OwnTracks Recorder before 1.0.5 contains a format string vulnerability in json_response() and related output functions that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code by storing a malicious tid value. Attackers can publish locations via POST /pub or MQTT with printf specifiers in tid, then read them back through GET /api/0/last to leak addresses and write memory.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_ssh() in src/dissectors/ec_ssh.c that copies a peer-supplied data_len without checking remaining packet bytes. A malicious SSHv1 client or server in an intercepted session can send a short packet with a large data_len to disclose up to 64 bytes of adjacent heap memory through captured credentials in the interface and log.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_mysql() in src/dissectors/ec_mysql.c that copies seed and password bytes without bounds checks. A malicious MySQL server or client can send truncated greeting or login packets to leak adjacent heap memory through hex-encoded output in the interface and log.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.2 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_vnc() in src/dissectors/ec_vnc.c that checks total packet length instead of remaining bytes. A malicious VNC server can send the authentication type and challenge in one short packet to leak up to 3 bytes of adjacent heap memory via the logged challenge.

Pika before 1.5.0 contains an uncontrolled resource allocation vulnerability that allows malicious brokers to exhaust client memory by declaring oversized frame payloads. Attackers can send frame headers declaring up to 4 GiB payloads, unchecked against frame_max, or very large message bodies to terminate consuming applications.

Supergateway 4.2.0 through 4.2.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in stdio-to-SSE mode that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the gateway via prototype-inherited sessionId values. Attackers can send a POST message request with sessionId set to toString or constructor, triggering an unhandled TypeError that terminates every attached MCP session.

desc: Netgate pfSense CE XMLRPC Incorrect Authorization Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Netgate pfSense. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within the XMLRPC endpoint. The issue results from incorrect authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code within the context of the root. Was ZDI-CAN-32353.

An authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed authenticated users to read review-thread data from private repositories they could not access. An attacker required an authenticated account, a readable repository and pull request to use as the request context, and target review-thread identifiers. The thread-preview endpoint resolved supplied identifiers without restricting them to the authorized pull request, exposing private file paths and, when positioning and diff data were available, source-code excerpts, commit identifiers, and line metadata without victim interaction. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases in the 3.21, 3.22 series and was fixed in versions 3.21.10, 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted pre-receive environment download URL. Exploitation required a clustered deployment using custom pre-receive hook environments and at least one peer Git server node. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, 3.20.12, and 3.19.16. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

A path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) was found in ansible-core's ansible-galaxy role installation. An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. A name containing "../" escapes that directory, and an absolute name replaces it entirely. Because ansible-galaxy processes transitive dependencies from an installed role's meta/requirements.yml, a malicious role publisher can cause attacker-supplied files to be written outside the operator's chosen roles directory when the operator installs the role, and, when --force is used, can cause an existing role directory outside that path to be removed and replaced. The impact is bounded by the invoking user's filesystem permissions and requires the operator to install the attacker-influenced content.

desc: A flaw was found in CRI-O. When the optional Linux LinkLogs feature is enabled, the host pod log directory is bind-mounted into a pod emptyDir and is intended to be read-only, but Linux ignores MS_RDONLY on the initial bind and the CRI mount stays writable. A non-privileged UID 0 container can place a symlink at a future kubelet log path so that privileged conmon later appends attacker-controlled log data to an existing host file. This is an append-only host integrity issue, not universal remote code execution; LinkLogs is not enabled by default.

desc: An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS System Control Interface ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU context. Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role. Even though it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active, there's zero value in not handling SMM. At that point, the only scenario where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides most of the re-configuration in that case). Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while L2 is active. Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when CR0.PG must be '0').

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync). However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns. If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer. This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command). Fix this by: 1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex in the synchronous command path. 2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding a NULL check before dereferencing.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: us122l: Add missing NULL check in usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() usb_stream_hwdep_mmap() reads us122l->sk.s and dereferences it without checking for NULL. The stream object is released by usb_stream_free(), which is reached through us122l_stop() both when the device is disconnected and when us122l_start() fails, and it leaves us122l->sk.s set to NULL. The hwdep file stays usable after that, so a later mmap() KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000010-0x0000000000000017] RIP: 0010:usb_stream_hwdep_mmap+0x107/0x890 sound/usb/usx2y/us122l.c:182 crashes while reading s->read_size, which sits at offset 0x10. That NULL is an expected state for this field: usb_stream_hwdep_vm_fault(), usb_stream_hwdep_poll(), usb_stream_hwdep_ioctl(), usb_stream_stop() and usb_stream_free() all test it before use. Only the mmap callback misses the check, so let it return -ENODEV, matching what the other hwdep mapping in usx2yhwdeppcm.c does when its shared buffer has not been allocated.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: us122l: Fix NULL dereference at hwdep open and release usb_stream_hwdep_open() and usb_stream_hwdep_release() pass the result of usb_ifnum_to_if() straight to usb_autopm_get_interface() and usb_autopm_put_interface(), without checking it for NULL. usb_ifnum_to_if() returns NULL once the device is gone, since usb_disable_device() clears udev->actconfig on disconnect. The hwdep file can outlive the disconnect: the card is released with snd_card_free_when_closed(), so a process that keeps the character device open reaches the driver's release callback after the USB configuration has been dropped, and interface_to_usbdev() then dereferences the NULL interface at offsetof(struct device, parent). The open callback has the same problem when it races with the disconnect. Check both lookups and fail the open with -ENODEV; in release, skip the runtime PM put when the interface is already gone and still run the rest of the per-file cleanup. Move the us122l->first bookkeeping after the checks so that a failed open no longer leaves a stale file pointer behind.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb, sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs of each direction. A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run before those pointers are set. While the stream is still being synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer: Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7] RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33 Call Trace: <IRQ> stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596 i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654 __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657 usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691 tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994 handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645 </IRQ> The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit loop. Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills and resubmits the streams.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized. A hwdep file descriptor can be shared among threads, or inherited across fork, so two SNDRV_HWDEP_IOCTL_DSP_LOAD requests for the same index can both observe the index as unloaded and enter the driver's callback concurrently, even though the device itself is opened exclusively. This breaks the assumption behind hw->dsp_loaded that a firmware index is loaded only once. For example, snd-usb-usx2y hits WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) in usx2y_async_seq04_init() and may allocate the US-428 sequence URBs twice. Serialize the check, the callback invocation and the bookkeeping with a per-hwdep mutex, so that the second request returns -EBUSY.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs. A rawmidi file that was already open can still be closed afterwards, and its close callback, bcd2000_midi_output_close(), calls usb_kill_urb() on midi_out_urb. The URB pointers are cleared on disconnect and their accesses are serialized with midi_lock, but bcd2000_midi_output_close() reads midi_out_urb without that lock. The check can therefore pass just before the pointer is cleared, and usb_kill_urb() then runs on the URB that has already been freed: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in usb_kill_urb+0x74/0x80 Read of size 8 at addr ffff8880078e7d40 usb_kill_urb bcd2000_midi_output_close close_substream rawmidi_release_priv snd_rawmidi_release Allocated by: usb_alloc_urb <- bcd2000_init_midi <- bcd2000_probe Freed by: usb_free_urb <- bcd2000_midi_free <- bcd2000_disconnect Take the lock in bcd2000_midi_output_close() and reference the URB with usb_get_urb() before releasing it. The URB then stays valid until usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect frees it in the meantime. usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded, and then creates the ALSA devices. If usx2y_in04_init() or usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up are left in place. The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user space may issue the same request again. The second attempt then enters usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb). The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock. Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning. The URBs are released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed. A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that path remains retryable.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected. This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

Out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the pixReadMemJp2kCore() function in Leptonica, located in jp2kio.c. The function retrieves the output dimensions only for component 0 and uses a common index to iterate through the buffers of all components. If the remaining components have smaller dimensions, the traversal exceeds the bounds of their sample buffers, which are allocated by OpenJPEG. When processing a specially crafted JPEG 2000 image, data read from adjacent dynamic memory may be incorporated into the pixels of the decoded image and result in information disclosure to anyone who can access the output.

desc: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to an untrusted proxy providing details that cause the broker to accept fake SSL information. This can be mitigated by following the documented requirements for PROXY listeners: It is very important that only trusted proxies are allowed to connect to any listener using the PROXY protocol, and that clients are not allowed to connect to the listener at all.

In Eclipse versions 1.5-1.6.13, 2.0.0-2.0.22 and 2.1.0-2.1.2, the client library libmosquitto does not reject Will messages with payloads greater than 65535 bytes when calling `mosquitto_will_set()` or `mosquitto_will_set_v5()`. This results in up to 65535 bytes of uninitialised heap memory being transmitted as the Will. This can be mitigated by only passing payloads with a maximum length of 65535 bytes.

A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0) allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1. For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files. Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.

desc: The BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 14.5.0. The function only verifies a nonce that is publicly exposed to any visitor who loads a BuddyPress page, but does not call `bp_activity_user_can_read()` to verify the user has permission to view the activity. desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) checked only that the caller was logged in, not the read_servers or manage_servers permission. Any authenticated user, including a user with no permissions, could download a diagnostic archive with the server log files, the host process list, a file system listing and the runtime server configuration. The runtime configuration contains the HTTP JWT signing secret and the message encryption key when they are set in the configuration. If HTTP is enabled, the user could use the signing secret to create tokens for any account, including root. This issue affects Apache Iggy: before 0.9.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

desc: MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group. A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members. The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. The impact is unauthorized disclosure of shared threat intelligence events and limited integrity modification of the sharing group record.

desc: Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames. Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory condition causing a Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued. This issue allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an unbounded allocation of memory and eventually an out-of-memory (OOM) condition. FIPS impact: no The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

desc: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. desc: Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer. Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length. CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a heap buffer overflow in the calling process. Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed. The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the defect can be reached. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Corruption mémoire; Déni de service; Zero-click

desc: Issue summary: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size. Impact summary: An attacker who can submit a CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message to an application that verifies it with CRL checking enabled can occupy a CPU core for seconds to minutes, causing Denial of Service. Applications that leave CRL checking disabled are not affected. CWE: CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity Description: With CRL checking enabled, OpenSSL compares each CRL distribution point of a certificate against the issuing distribution point of every candidate CRL. For a nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point, the full name is the CRL issuer name with the relative name appended. Since the change that deferred this computation, crl_crldp_check() rebuilds that full name for each candidate CRL and frees it again. CMS_verify() and PKCS7_verify() take both the distribution points and the candidate CRLs from the message, and this scoring runs before any signature is checked. An application is exposed only if it sets X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK on the store and does not pass CMS_NOCRL or PKCS7_NOCRL; CRL checking is off by default. In TLS the CRLs come from the local store, so a peer controls only the distribution point count. The cost grows with the product of the distribution point count, the CRL count and the issuer name length, all chosen by the message author; a few hundred kilobytes can occupy a CPU core for tens of seconds. Verification still fails as it should, with no crash, no incorrect result and no memory growth. Requiring CRL checking is what limits the severity. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in genAVValueHTML() that allows attackers who can store Attribute View asset values to inject script through an unescaped image src attribute. Attackers can store an image URL containing a double quote and onerror handler that executes OS commands via Node.js in the desktop app when victims open the bound note or row attribute panel.

SiYuan from 3.3.0 before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject HTML via unescaped checkbox column names in Gallery and Kanban AttributeView renderers. Attackers can share a crafted .sy.zip document whose rendering in the Electron desktop client with nodeIntegration enabled executes Node.js and host OS commands.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-44670, because renderAVAttribute() inserts an Attribute View name unescaped into the database row attribute panel header. Attackers who can persist the name, such as via the setAttrViewName action, can inject an onerror handler that runs OS commands through Node.js when a desktop user opens the panel.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 persists a table block's caption attribute into IAL properties without HTML sanitization, causing stored cross-site scripting upon import or sync. Attackers can inject an entity-encoded caption with an onerror handler that executes in the Electron client's nodeIntegration context to achieve remote code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 uses an incomplete deny-list in IsSensitivePath that omits shell-initialization files such as .zshenv and .bash_profile, as well as ~/.local. Authenticated administrators can call /api/file/copyFile with an absolute destination outside the workspace to write payloads there, which execute as the user on the next shell or login.

vLLM before 0.33.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious model publishers to redirect the served model and tokenizer by setting speculators_config verifier.name_or_path in config.json. Attackers can point this field at another local checkpoint directory to leak its tokenizer vocabulary via unauthenticated /detokenize requests and gain query access to private models.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Traversée de répertoire

desc: vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware never enforced allowedRoles. Attackers can generate a super admin password reset link via org-users endpoints to take over the instance, or read and modify SSO client secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the unauthenticated dynamic client registration endpoint. Attackers can impersonate trusted applications on a consent screen lacking unverified-client warnings or redirect host display, obtaining tokens to read and write victim tables and records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Fuite d'informations

desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local flags. Attackers can create sources or bases with these flags to expose user, token and integration tables, then read and modify records including user roles.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical column names. Attackers can supply a hidden column's physical name or the unchecked sub-group parameter to the public group-by endpoint to reveal hidden values, counts, and column existence.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Fuite d'informations

desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source id when adding a source. Because NcConnectionMgrv2 caches connections by bare source id, attackers can reflect the victim's cached database schema and read, update, and insert records through their own base models.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. Attackers holding an unexpired reset link, such as from prior mailbox access, can set a new password and regain control of the account.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by supplying arbitrary primary keys. Attackers with the share link can request attachment downloads and many-to-many or has-many link listings for excluded records to obtain their attachment files and linked record identities.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the internal batch endpoint. Attackers can name a writable decoy table on the batch envelope and target a read-only source table in dataUpdate, dataInsert or dataDelete sub-operations to modify or destroy records.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter. Anonymous share-link holders can enumerate auto-increment primary keys against the has-many, many-to-many, one-to-many and link-to-another-record routes to read linked records of filtered-out rows.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Fuite d'informations

desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs. Attackers can send a consent link to a signed-in victim so either consent button runs script in the NocoDB origin, stealing the session token for account takeover.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM or Negotiate schemes. Attackers can open many short-lived connections that each allocate a dedicated backend transport never released, exhausting memory, file descriptors and backend connections.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers to bypass the media action allowlist using scoped method names in Markdown image URLs. Attackers can chain actions like self::addMetaFile into static calls such as Process::fromShellCommandline to read files and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers to grant super-admin rights by nesting access maps under a YAML merge key. Attackers with admin.users.create or api.users.write can submit '<<' keys, for example via PATCH /api/v1/users/<self>, that bypass super-grant filtering and gain full site control.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers with admin.users.update to take over super admin accounts by disabling the super-granting group. Attackers can set the group's enabled field to false via the Flex user-groups form, then reset the victim's password through the user-accounts form to gain super admin access.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying client-controlled storage keys. Attackers can abuse the create form username, cross-type form flash replay, or __META storage key rename to gain super-admin accounts or delete account files.
tags: Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Élévation de privilèges

desc: Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset tokens through unfiltered account serialization. Attackers can embed a Flex form for the user-accounts directory in a page or query the Flex API with admin.users.read to obtain super admin credentials and take over the account.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page accessor setters such as filePath(). Attackers can repoint page objects or overwrite the assets collections to render private keys and the API signing secret, then forge a super-admin API token.

Grav 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 resolves Flex sort and filter field names by first calling them as public methods, so a field named delete invokes FlexObject::delete() without any permission check. Authenticated users with only list access can send GET /api/v1/flex-objects/user-accounts?sort=delete requests to delete every account, then use the reopened API first-run setup to create a super admin.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows page editors to escape the Twig sandbox by sending requests with a Host: pages header. Attackers can write configuration YAML through page folders and media .meta.yaml sidecars to register an unsandboxed Twig namespace and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

desc: Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable Cache-Control header. When a shared cache such as Apache mod_cache stores Set-Cookie responses, an attacker can lure a user signed in through the front-end login to open a media URL with a unique query string, then request that URL to receive the cached session cookie and take over the session.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because UserCollection::count() uses an unescaped glob() pattern. On installs whose path contains brackets or a backslash, the account count returns zero, so attackers can send requests to POST /api/v1/auth/setup or the classic admin registration form to create or overwrite administrator accounts.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto header. Attackers can send a forgot-password request with a crafted scheme value so the emailed reset link points to their host, capturing the token to take over accounts including super admins.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to fill the disk by varying the HTTP Host header. Attackers can send requests with distinct Host values to create per-host compiled configuration, blueprint, language and page index caches, causing session, upload and logging failures.
