tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Corruption mémoire; Déni de service; Zero-click

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains an integer overflow in the client GDI handling of accumulated drawing-order bounds: wrapped INT32 coordinates yield a zero-width clip region that causes clipping to be skipped in gdi_FillRect. A malicious RDP server can send many ORDER_BOUNDS orders followed by an OPAQUE_RECT order to trigger a heap out-of-bounds write past the client's drawing bitmap, potentially leading to code execution.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Corruption mémoire; Zero-click

desc: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the shadow server's fast-path input handlers in fastpath.c that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject input before activation. Attackers can negotiate TLS-only RDP, skip Confirm Active, and send Fast-Path Input Event PDUs to inject keystrokes and mouse movement into the host X11 session via XTEST.

FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a reachable assertion in remdesk_server_thread that allows authenticated clients to abort freerdp-shadow-cli by sending oversized remdesk messages. Attackers can send one message longer than 4096 bytes with a shorter declared PDU length, forcing Stream_Seek past capacity and terminating every served session.

FreeRDP 2.11.2 before 3.33.0 contains unbounded resource consumption in the Progressive codec because progressive_decompress() resets the tile update batch only when frameId changes. A malicious RDP server can repeat RDPGFX_CAPROGRESSIVE WireToSurface2 commands with a constant frameId to cause unbounded memory growth, quadratic CPU cost, a heap out-of-bounds write on tile-cache allocation failure, and client crashes.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service; Corruption mémoire; Zero-click

desc: FreeRDP from 3.10.0 before 3.33.0 contains an invalid free vulnerability in rdg.c because the websocket context pointer shares a union with chunked transfer-encoding decoder state. A malicious RD Gateway answering the data channel with chunked encoding can control the overwritten pointer via chunk sizes, causing rdg_free to free an attacker-influenced value and crash the client.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Corruption mémoire; Déni de service; Zero-click

desc: FreeRDP from 3.0.0 before 3.33.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in cert_write_server_certificate_v1() that computes the proprietary certificate signature over a freed stream buffer after reallocation. Clients negotiating Standard RDP Security with many static channels against servers using 3072- or 4096-bit keys trigger freed heap reads, producing invalid certificate signatures.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Corruption mémoire; Zero-click

desc: FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read in WinPR's save_png_to_buffer(), which selects an RGB PNG color type for 9–16 bpp images but fills only 2 bytes per pixel per row. A malicious RDP server can send 9–16 bpp CF_DIB clipboard data that, when a local application requests image/png, yields a PNG containing adjacent client heap memory.

HKUDS nanobot from 0.1.4 before 0.4.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in the OpenAI Codex provider that retries authenticated requests without TLS certificate or hostname verification. Attackers able to intercept the connection can trigger a certificate failure and impersonate the endpoint to steal bearer tokens, read request contents, or alter responses.

ImageMagick 7.0.0 before 7.1.2-35 and before 6.9.13-60 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the distributed pixel cache server, which transmits pixel and metadata content in cleartext. Attackers who can observe traffic between a DPC client and server can read transmitted image data.

Parse Server 3.10.0 before 8.6.123 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.4 contains an authentication bypass in the Google Play Games authentication adapter, which does not verify that the supplied player ID belongs to the presented access token. Attackers can sign in with their own Google Play Games credential while claiming another user's player ID to take over that account or link that player ID to their own account.

Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 matches $in, $nin, $all and $containedBy constraints in LiveQuery with a cost proportional to the product of the constraint list size and the saved array size. A client that can subscribe to a class and save objects in it can use large lists and arrays to block the event loop for seconds or longer, stalling LiveQuery and, when it runs in the same process, Parse Server.

SiYuan before 3.8.11 uses DejaVu sync code that accepts a non-hexadecimal 40-byte remote index ID from WebDAV responses and joins it into the repository indexes path unchecked, allowing path traversal. An on-path attacker altering plaintext HTTP WebDAV sync responses can overwrite a workspace data file, such as a .sy note, with compressed index data.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Traversée de répertoire

desc: SiYuan from 3.8.0 before 3.8.11 contains a lockout bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to brute-force publish passwords by forging client-computable publish-auth-<ID> cookies. Attackers can compute SHA-256(ID + candidate) locally and send it on content requests like /api/filetree/getDoc to guess passwords without throttling and read protected documents.

SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.11 contains a DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerability in the AI agent chat panel, which renders final and saved assistant replies into innerHTML without HTML sanitisation. Attackers influencing model replies via indirect prompt injection or a configured model endpoint can inject event-handler markup, executing OS commands through Node.js integration in desktop local-kernel mode.

SiYuan before 3.8.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM event handlers by storing handler-named block attributes such as onmouseover. Attackers can share crafted .sy.zip packages or Markdown files whose attributes reach renderCustom or the unsanitised preview pane, executing OS commands via Node integration in the desktop app.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability where WebDAV sync error formatting skips HTML escaping for certain malformed-response errors, passing raw markup to the Electron notification renderer. A network attacker who alters a cleartext HTTP WebDAV response can inject event-handler markup that, when the victim manually starts sync, executes JavaScript with Node integration as the logged-in user.

SiYuan from 3.6.2 before 3.8.10 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows admin token holders to read files outside the workspace because the globalCopyFiles and workspaceCopyFiles denylist omits /home, /mnt, /media, and /snap. Attackers can copy other users' SSH authorized_keys, Docker and AWS configs, or mounted files into the workspace and retrieve them via the getFile API.

SiYuan from 3.8.6-beta.1 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows read-only publish users (RoleReader) to modify persistent workspace configuration via /api/system/getChangelog. Attackers can send POST requests through the publish service proxy, even anonymously when basic authentication is disabled, to persist ShowChangelog = false to conf.json.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: SiYuan 3.8.8 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect permission assignment vulnerability that creates workspace directories with mode 0755 and conf.json with mode 0644, exposing the cleartext AccessAuthCode administrator credential. Local users able to traverse the SiYuan user's home path can read it and authenticate as administrator via Basic authentication, for example calling /api/system/setAPIToken to change the API token.

vLLM 0.21.0 before 0.28.0, when using the V1 model runner, contains a state aliasing flaw in ThinkingBudgetStateHolder.sync_batch(), whose SWAP branch copies thinking-budget state to the destination batch row without removing the source entry. Attackers submitting requests with thinking_token_budget can force the reasoning-end token sequence into a concurrent co-batched request's output during a mixed batch reorder.

vLLM 0.3.0 before 0.30.0 contains a response amplification vulnerability in the OpenAI-compatible API server's shared RequestValidationError handler, which renders every Pydantic validation error, each of which can include the full offending input, in its HTTP 400 response. Unauthenticated attackers can send a malformed request to endpoints such as POST /v1/responses to trigger a disproportionately large error response that consumes server CPU and memory and can disrupt downstream clients and proxies.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: vLLM 0.16.0 before 0.21.0 leaks token data between users when the V1 model runner uses async scheduling with pipeline parallelism, because non-last pipeline ranks never write generated tokens to token_ids_cpu and reset num_tokens_no_spec each step. When the fallback path is triggered, such as by mixed prefill/decode batches, stale tokens from a prior request in the same batch slot become model input and are written to the KV cache, exposing fragments of one user's context in another user's response.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authentication bypass in the ForwardAuth middleware because connection isolation for NTLM and Negotiate credentials checks only the Authorization header, not Proxy-Authorization. Unauthenticated attackers can send such credentials in Proxy-Authorization to reuse a shared authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity via authResponseHeaders, and access backends as that user.

Traefik 3.1.0 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the Compress middleware, which creates zstd encoders with library default options that retain about 18 MiB of state per response until it is fully written. Unauthenticated remote attackers can open many concurrent requests and read responses slowly to exhaust memory and crash Traefik.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contains a client certificate authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider because, on hosts shared by multiple Ingresses using auth-tls-secret, Ssl-Client-* headers are built per Ingress while the TLS handshake uses the first Ingress's settings. Unauthenticated remote attackers can obtain Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a client-chosen subject and issuer for an unverified certificate, or inject Ssl-Client-* headers directly, presenting forged identities to backends that trust the proxy.
family: Virtualisation / Cloud / Conteneurs; Serveur web / applicatif

desc: Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authorization bypass because the sanitizePath entry point option leaves dot-segments carrying path parameters, such as /..;x/, unresolved when matching routers and applying middlewares. Unauthenticated attackers can send requests like /public/..;x/admin to a parameter-stripping backend shared with a protected router, bypassing authentication or authorization middlewares to reach protected resources.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Traversée de répertoire

desc: Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contain a denial of service vulnerability in the BasicAuth middleware, which does not limit password length before MD5-crypt ($apr1$, $1$) hashing. Unauthenticated attackers can send passwords up to the entry point maxHeaderBytes limit (1 MiB by default), consuming excessive CPU per request and degrading availability.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Hono from 4.13.11 before 4.13.18 contains a middleware bypass vulnerability in serveStatic that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip prefix middleware by exploiting a second path decode when allowPercentInPath is enabled. Attackers can send malformed percent-encoded sequences so the router matches an encoded path while serveStatic serves the real file, bypassing authentication checks.

Hono from 4.12.16 before 4.13.18 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the bodyLimit() middleware that retains every transfer chunk as a separate array. Unauthenticated attackers can send a within-limit request body in one-byte chunks to create millions of retained objects, terminating Bun or Node.js processes.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Hono from 4.5.1 before 4.13.18 contains a validation bypass vulnerability in validator('json') and validator('form') that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip validation by formatting Content-Type parameters differently. Attackers can add whitespace before semicolons, trailing semicolons, or underscored parameter names so validators receive empty objects while handlers still read rejected fields.

Hono from 4.13.16 before 4.13.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in mount() and app.mount() that forwards an incorrect path when a custom getPath adds a prefix. Unauthenticated attackers can request crafted paths that the mounted application resolves differently, reaching routes protected by path-scoped middleware such as authentication checks.

OpenWrt LuCI luci-app-unbound through 26.288.56989~75a306d contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the Unbound Configure page inserts the dhcp.odhcpd.leasetrigger value into a warning notification without escaping. Users with delegated network configuration access can store an HTML event handler in that option through the permitted uci RPC, which executes in an administrator's browser session when the page renders.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read SELECT-hidden edge endpoints through InOverride/OutOverride error messages. Attackers with CREATE and UPDATE permission on an edge table can re-RELATE an existing edge with mismatched endpoints to recover stored in/out record ids despite row- or field-level restrictions.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the remote HTTP client router that passes raw model names to Url::join during ML export. Attackers can supply an absolute URL as the model name in ExportMl or ExportBytesMl commands to redirect authenticated requests and capture session tokens.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted subjects to execute arbitrary queries by calling the JavaScript surrealdb.query() bridge. Attackers permitted to run a specific script can bypass the Capabilities::allows_query() gate in the query module to execute unrestricted queries beyond their predefined operations.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a query injection vulnerability that allows low-privilege or anonymous users to inject AQL or SQL by supplying unescaped parameters to ArangoDB and Snowflake queries. Attackers can execute published queries with crafted parameter values to bypass filters, read entire datasources, and modify or delete all stored documents.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows workspace-scoped builders to access other workspaces' backups by supplying a foreign backupId. Attackers can substitute predictable backup IDs in backup download, import, update, or delete routes to steal archives, restore victim data into their workspace, or delete backups.

Budibase server from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view users and anonymous visitors to access entire base tables by passing a view id to the /api/:viewId/rows routes. Attackers can read, export, modify, and delete rows outside the view filter, including hidden columns, or read the full table unauthenticated through PUBLIC views.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a broken object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table write access to reference other tenants' files by supplying arbitrary attachment keys on row save. Attackers can inject a victim app's attachment key into a row, then update or delete the row to delete that object from the shared APPS bucket or read it via presigned URLs.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the bulkDestroy function that allows authenticated users to delete rows from any workspace table by supplying foreign row IDs. Attackers with TABLE WRITE on one table can send row _id values from other tables to the DELETE /api/:sourceId/rows endpoint, causing data loss and workspace metadata deletion.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with table read permission to execute JavaScript by injecting Handlebars js helpers into row search query values. Attackers can submit base64-encoded JavaScript through the search endpoint, which enrichSearchContext() runs in an isolated-vm sandbox, to read OAuth2 access and refresh tokens of SSO users or cause denial of service.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve legacy LiteLLM credentials by querying the public settings endpoint. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests to /api/global/configs/public to obtain liteLLM.keyId and secretKey, enabling unauthorized use of tenant LiteLLM resources.

Budibase Server from 3.39.18 before 4.0.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to erase MongoDB query filters by supplying __proto__ as a dynamic JSON key in PUBLIC queries. Attackers can send a single request to the query execution endpoint, reducing the filter to {} to read, update, or delete every document in the collection.

Budibase from 3.41.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to take over password-less global Builder accounts via unverified-email OIDC/SSO account linking. Attackers can assert a victim's email with email_verified=false at a trusted IdP, bypassing the isAccountLinkable allowlist to control all apps, datasources, and automations.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin Creator or app-builder users to read pending invite bearer codes via GET /api/global/users/invites. Attackers can submit a stolen code with a chosen password to the public /api/global/users/invite/accept endpoint, hijacking invited identities up to global admin.

Budibase Server before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass in its single-row read and attachment endpoints, which fetch rows by ID without enforcing the requesting view's row filter. Authenticated users with read access to a filtered view can request GET /api/:viewId/rows/:rowId or GET /api/:viewId/rows/:rowId/attachment/:columnName with a hidden row ID to retrieve that row's data and attachments.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a JSON injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JSON structure into S3 delete and Google Sheets row fields via unescaped template parameters. Attackers can submit crafted parameters to the queries endpoint to add extra Key entries, deleting chosen S3 objects or overriding Sheets row columns.

actix-multipart (actix-web) before 0.8.7 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the MultipartForm extractor that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory or file descriptors by sending unlimited parts. Attackers can stream many zero-byte parts uncounted by total_limit and memory_limit, pinning 128 KiB buffers or opening temporary files to crash workers.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: actix-http before 3.20.4 contains a response desynchronization vulnerability in its HTTP/1 client response decoder, which reads bodies on 1xx, 204 and 304 responses based on Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding headers. Servers sending such responses with framing headers cause awc clients to consume subsequent keep-alive responses, causing request failures or misattributing responses across users in proxies.

Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in object.to_json that allows template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit by serializing into an unbounded MemoryStream. Attackers can repeatedly apply object.to_json to escape-heavy strings in a tiny template, amplifying output to multi-gigabyte heap allocations and causing denial of service.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows template authors to bypass LimitToString by rendering a ScriptObject with many members. Attackers can supply a small template whose ScriptObject.ToString concatenates large member values without length tracking, allocating multi-gigabyte strings and causing memory exhaustion.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Scriban and Scriban.Signed before 7.6.0 allow template authors to bypass the LimitToString string length limit because the string.literal, string.base64_encode, html.escape, html.newline_to_br, html.url_encode, and html.url_escape builtins lack allocation guards. An attacker who can supply a small template can repeatedly call these builtins under the default TemplateContext to force multi-gigabyte allocations and exhaust host memory.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a state isolation vulnerability because TemplateContext.Reset() does not clear the Tags dictionary holding array.cycle and math.random state. Attackers supplying templates to a reused context can observe or influence cycle positions and random sequences across renders, and accumulate unbounded cycle entries to exhaust memory.

Scriban before 7.6.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass LoopLimit by supplying large JSON input to object.from_json. Attackers can pass a flat JSON array or object with hundreds of thousands of elements, which JsonElementExtensions materializes without loop checks, exhausting CPU and memory.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: justhtml before 3.17.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in decode_entities_in_text that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash parsing via non-ASCII Unicode digits in numeric character references. Attackers can submit a payload like &#² in HTML text or attributes, causing an uncaught ValueError from int() that aborts JustHTML() and stream() parsing.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Déni de service

desc: Nodemailer 9.1.0 before 10.4.1 lowercases recipient domains with JavaScript toLowerCase() in _normalizeAddress before UTS-46 mapping, which converts U+1E9E and word-final U+03A3 differently than WHATWG/UTS-46 validators. An unprivileged attacker can submit an address an application's allow-list approves, causing invites or shared links to reach an attacker-registered domain.

AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in RelaysController::updateAction that allows any authenticated user to modify shared relays and delete other stations' relay associations. Attackers can POST a relay base_url to /internal/relays to rename the relay, wipe StationRemote rows of unmanaged stations, and spoof public now-playing data.

AzuraCast before 0.24.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the StationPublicApi middleware that allows any authenticated user to access non-public stations without per-station permissions. Attackers can change the station_id path parameter to list and download on-demand media, read schedule data, and submit song requests to unauthorized stations.

ToolJet from 3.8.0 before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated builders to modify queries in view-only apps by supplying cross-app query IDs. Attackers can send PATCH requests to /api/data-queries/versions/:versionId naming an editable app version with another app's query ID, then run the overwritten query using that app's data source connection.

ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows Builders with only data source Delete permission to update global data sources via the PUT /api/data-sources endpoint. Attackers can change a REST data source base URL so later query executions send stored Bearer credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS is missing the ValidateDataSourceGuard on the dependent-queries route of the data-sources controller and does not scope the datasource lookup to the caller's organization. An authenticated admin or builder with dataSourceDelete can request /api/data-sources/dependent-queries/<datasource_uuid> to confirm a datasource exists in another organization and learn its dependent-query count.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated builders to read, modify, or delete other organizations' app-builder components, pages, and events. Attackers can target their own app/version in the URL to pass ValidAppGuard, then supply victim resource ids that services query without appVersionId or organizationId scoping.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in QueryAuthGuard that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute queries from unreleased app versions. Attackers can POST to the data-queries run endpoint with a draft query ID from any public app to execute unpublished queries against connected datasources.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass in instance-level Google SSO because the id_token audience is not verified when no Google OAuth client ID is configured, the shipped default. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a Google-signed id_token minted for their own OAuth client to /api/sso/sign-in/common/google without an organizationId, obtaining a session as any existing user with the matching email.

ToolJet from 3.20.84 before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the instance-level SSO sign-in path that hardcodes signup as enabled, ignoring all signup-disable controls. Any user with an account on the configured GitHub or Google identity provider can sign in via the OAuth endpoint to obtain an admin session in a newly created workspace.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Contournement d'authentification

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows users with TEST_CONNECTION ability to exfiltrate organization secrets by resolving secret placeholders in test-connection options. Attackers can point the host and port at a listener they control and set the password option to a secrets template, causing the server to send the plaintext secret to them.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass in the internal database (TJDB) PostgREST proxy, which grants proxy access to every logged-in user and derives the database role and schema from the client-supplied tj-workspace-id header. Any authenticated workspace member can send requests to /api/tooljet-db/proxy/<tableId> to read and modify TJDB tables, bypassing app, query, and table permissions, and in SQL-mode-disabled (Cloud) deployments can access all tenants' tables.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a cross-workspace authorization bypass in the organization-users archive and unarchive endpoints, which take the target organizationId from the request body without validating it against the caller's authorized workspaces. An admin of any workspace who knows a target organization-user ID and workspace UUID can archive or unarchive users in other tenants' workspaces, locking them out of those workspaces and tampering with the audit trail.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated same-organization users to invoke OAuth2 authorization on data sources they cannot configure. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/data-sources/:id/authorize_oauth2 to bind attacker-controlled OAuth credentials or overwrite token state for foreign data sources.

ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in getVersionsByEnvironment that allows authenticated users to read another organization's application versions due to missing organizationId scoping. Attackers can request the app-environments versions route with their own priority-1 production environment id and a victim app_id to retrieve the victim's version list and structure.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view-only workspace users to execute queries in restricted environments by supplying an arbitrary environmentId. Attackers can call the data-queries run endpoint for draft app versions to execute queries with stored datasource credentials, exposing development or staging data.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read cross-workspace files by requesting a known File UUID. Attackers can request GET /api/files/:id with another workspace's File UUID to retrieve stored file bytes, such as avatars, without parent resource authorization checks.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privilege app/query viewers to obtain plaintext workspace secrets by running REST queries. Attackers can execute queries via POST /data-queries/:id/run whose URL params or non-redacted headers reference secrets, reading resolved values from metadata.request despite lacking decrypted constants access.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to recover plaintext workspace secret constants through OAuth URL generation. Attackers can send POST /api/data-sources/fetch-oauth2-base-url with {{secrets.*}} in source_options and arbitrary organization_id and environment_id to receive secrets, including other workspaces' secrets, in the returned authorization URL.

ToolJet before 3.21.94-beta contains an authentication bypass in its server OAuth SSO sign-in module, which resolves Google and Git SSO logins solely by the provider-asserted email without checking email_verified or binding the SSO subject. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a trusted-issuer token carrying a victim's unverified email to the SSO callback to obtain the victim's session, including admin accounts.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated End Users to execute data queries of apps in other organizations via POST /api/data-queries/:id/run. Attackers can supply a target data-query id and runtime resolvedOptions to run queries with the datasource's decrypted credentials, reading cross-tenant query results.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to reuse expired JWTs because the passport-jwt strategy sets ignoreExpiration to true. Attackers holding a leaked tj_auth_token can keep sessions alive through auto-extended expiry and two-year cookies to persistently access victim accounts.

Tornado before 6.6.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in StaticFileHandler on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to read NTFS Alternate Data Streams by appending :streamname to URL paths. Attackers can request stream paths that pass the get_absolute_path and _check_in_root prefix checks to read hidden stream content, such as stored secrets or Zone.Identifier source data.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Traversée de répertoire; Fuite d'informations

desc: LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the QuickDraft Livewire component that allows any authenticated user to create posts without the post.create permission. Attackers such as self-registered Subscriber accounts can submit the dashboard Quick Draft widget to inject draft posts, bypassing the PostPolicy check enforced by PostController.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in SettingObserver that writes full Setting models, including plaintext secret option_value fields, into the action_logs table. Users holding only actionlog.view can read API keys, SMTP passwords, and OAuth client secrets through the action log API without settings permissions.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by abusing the unvalidated ai_ollama_base_url setting. Once a settings.edit user points the Ollama base URL internally, any post.create user can call /admin/ai/generate-seo with provider=ollama to fetch internal data reflected in SEO fields.

LaraDashboard before 1.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in module.json providers and composer.json psr-4 namespace parsing that derives destination folder names without excluding traversal characters. Attackers with module.create permission can upload a crafted module ZIP to write PHP files into the public directory, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution.

Coder 2.9.0 before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.12, 2.35.0 before 2.35.9, 2.36.0 before 2.36.7, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.3 contains a nil pointer dereference in the tailnet coordinator, which reads UpdateSelf.Node fields during authorization without checking that Node is set. An authenticated user or workspace agent token holder can send a CoordinateRequest with UpdateSelf present but Node empty to crash coderd, disconnecting all users on the affected replica.

Coder 2.29.17 before 2.29.27, 2.32.7 before 2.33.0, 2.33.8 before 2.34.0, 2.34.2 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows malicious template authors to steal session tokens because coder open app substitutes $SESSION_TOKEN into template-defined external app URLs without validating scheme or destination. Attackers can define an external app URL or IDE link pointing to an attacker server so users running coder open app leak their token, enabling impersonation of shared users or administrators.

desc: The Warehouse Cargo theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in versions up to, and including, 2.7.4 via the warehouse_cargo_install_and_activate_plugin() AJAX handler. The handler is registered on wp_ajax_ but performs no nonce verification and no capability check, allowing any authenticated user to supply an attacker-controlled URL that the server fetches, writes into wp-content/plugins/ with file_put_contents(), extracts with unzip_file() (which does not filter file extensions), and then activates via activate_plugin(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to upload arbitrary files on the affected site's server which makes remote code execution possible.

A valid nonce required for form submission can be freely obtained by any unauthenticated visitor via the publicly accessible REST route 'Emsfb/v1/nonce/refresh', which is registered with no permission check, enabling the full attack chain without any credentials.

desc: The Lenix Leads Collector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Field Name in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable because the plugin's CF7 integration accepts and stores any extra field name not defined in the CF7 form — including HTML/JS payloads — submitted by an unauthenticated user via a public CF7 form submission, with the raw field name later echoed unescaped in two separate admin-side sinks.

The WebP Express plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Malformed Bcrypt Salt in all versions up to, and including, 0.25.15. This is due to insufficient validation of the attacker-supplied `salt` POST parameter in the `runAccessChecks()` function, which passes the unvalidated salt directly to PHP's `crypt()` — causing it to return an empty string when the salt contains characters outside the valid bcrypt alphabet `[./0-9A-Za-z]` — and then loosely compares the resulting empty string against the attacker-controlled `api-key-crypted` POST parameter using `==`, allowing an empty submission to match and satisfy the check. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the web service API-key authentication check and upload arbitrary image files to the cloud-conversion endpoint, where they persist at a predictable, publicly reachable path under `wp-content/webp-express/webp-images/wpc/`. The 'Require api-key to be crypted in transfer?' whitelist setting does not mitigate this bypass, as it only gates the plaintext API-key comparison branch and has no effect on the crypted-key branch containing the vulnerable logic.

The handler accepts a `wc_order` parameter from the query string, loads the corresponding WooCommerce order without any authentication, nonce, session, capability, or ownership check, and — when the order is paid — issues a 302 redirect to `get_return_url($order)`, whose `Location` header embeds the order's secret `order_key`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to harvest order keys for arbitrary orders (regardless of payment method) and then use those keys against the WooCommerce order-received, order-pay and download endpoints to read the associated customer's PII, including billing name, street address, phone number, email, purchased items, and totals.

desc: The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'nickname / display_name (via WP core profile form); thread[body] carries the [quote data-userid=..] trigger' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. @fastify/middie is the plugin that adds Express-style middleware support to the Fastify web framework. In versions 9.3.6 through 9.3.9, a route or mount path written without a leading slash inside a plugin registered under a prefix is handled inconsistently: the middleware is mounted with a separating slash after the prefix, while the route is concatenated directly onto the prefix, so a request to the concatenated path reaches the route handler without running the middleware mounted for it. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.10, and users should upgrade to 9.3.10 or later. As a workaround, begin all route and mount paths with a slash, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.3 before 4.0.14, the plugin decodes certain percent-encoded characters in the request path that Express would otherwise keep encoded, including the Unicode line separator and paragraph separator characters, and leaves them raw. A JavaScript regular expression treats those two characters as line terminators, so a regular-expression mount path that relies on the dot metacharacter fails to match a request containing them while Fastify's own router still routes the request to its handler, and the middleware mounted on that regular-expression path is therefore skipped. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on routes guarded by a regular-expression mount; string mount paths are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, use string mount paths, avoid the dot metacharacter in regular-expression mounts by using a character class or the dotAll flag, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.7 before 4.0.14, when middleware is mounted on a nested array of mount paths the plugin rewrites only the top level of the array, so paths inside a nested array are not adjusted for a plugin registered under a prefix and the middleware never runs for them, a nested regular-expression mount keeps its global or sticky flag and is matched statefully so it is skipped on alternating requests, a nested regular expression is not matched case-insensitively when case sensitivity is disabled, and nested dynamic paths are not covered by the earlier empty-segment check. An attacker can use any of these to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, flatten mount path arrays before passing them to the plugin, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.5 before 4.0.14, a mount path that begins with an Express 5 optional leading segment written as a group is treated as relative and has a slash prepended when it is joined to the plugin prefix, which changes what the pattern matches so the middleware ends up mounted on a path that no longer corresponds to the real request paths. The middleware therefore never runs for requests that match the intended routes, while the Fastify routes still resolve to their handlers. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, mount the middleware on each path spelling explicitly, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.
tags: Pré-authentification à distance; Contrôle d'accès défaillant; Contournement d'authentification

desc: @fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, a request with an empty dynamic route parameter reaches a Fastify route handler while middleware mounted for that path inside an Express Router or sub-application is skipped, because Fastify's router accepts an empty value where Express requires a non-empty one, and an unanchored regular-expression mount passed to the plugin is bypassed the same way. An earlier fix covered only the mount paths passed to the plugin directly, not middleware mounted inside a routed Express application. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, with the practical impact depending on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, mount the middleware on a static parent path, or require non-empty values in the route params schema.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, when an application enables case-insensitive routing, middleware mounted on a path can still be skipped in two cases: a string mount path or plugin prefix containing a Unicode character whose case folding differs from a plain lowercase conversion fails to match the lowercased request path, and a matcher that stays case-sensitive inside an Express Router or application, such as a regular expression without the ignore-case flag or an explicitly case-sensitive router, only matches its own casing. In both cases a request reaches the Fastify route handler while the path-scoped middleware does not run. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, and only applications that enable case-insensitive routing are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, avoid such Unicode characters in mount paths, and match case-insensitively inside Express routers and applications.

The Apache Airflow TaskFlow decorators @task.bash, @task.sql, @task.analytics, @task.kubernetes_cmd and the common.ai decorators (@task.llm, @task.agent, @task.llm_sql, @task.llm_branch, @task.llm_file_analysis, @task.llm_schema_compare) rendered Jinja templates a second time after the task runner had already rendered them, so any value copied into env, op_args, op_kwargs or the returned prompt, command or SQL was evaluated as a template on the worker. desc: An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl handling in the **Samba** package. The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

desc: A server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw was found in KubeVirt's decentralized live migration. The connectURL field of a VirtualMachineInstanceMigration object is not validated at admission, and the privileged synchronization-controller dials the attacker-specified URL. Connection and DNS errors from the dial are exposed in a condition readable in the tenant's namespace. A user with the kubevirt.io:migrate role (a role designed for tenant delegation) can use this behavior as a blind network-reconnaissance oracle to determine the existence and connectivity of internal hosts and ports from the controller's network vantage, including services isolated from the tenant by network policy. TLS certificate pinning prevents session completion with non-KubeVirt hosts, limiting the impact to information disclosure of internal network topology; no data content, integrity, or availability impact is possible.

desc: A flaw was found in spice-server. A malicious SPICE client can send a message header declaring an arbitrarily large message body. On hosts with sufficient free memory, the same technique can instead hold large amounts of memory per connection. Exploitation requires network access to the SPICE port; credential requirements depend on the server's authentication configuration.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in the instance file transfer API in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and write arbitrary host block or character devices, compromise the host, and hang file transfer requests via importing device nodes or named pipes outside /dev in an image or backup and opening them on a stopped instance.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in image and backup metadata handling in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2, 5.21.10, 5.0.12, 4.0.16 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and overwrite arbitrary host files, access other projects' data, and block the daemon via importing device nodes, hard links, symlinks, or named pipes.

Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

A vulnerability has been found in code-projects Simple Laundry System 1.0. This affects an unknown function of the file viewdetailforuser.php. The manipulation of the argument serviceId leads to sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

product: Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP
desc: The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
affected: magazine3 Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP
ranges: magazine3 Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP

product: Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms
desc: The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy_files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy_files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.
affected: crmperks Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms
ranges: crmperks Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms

product: Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder
desc: The Forminator Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Approval Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.3 via the forminator_replace_custom_form_data() function. This is due to the function expanding the {all_fields} merge tag before {account_approval_link}, so a submitter-supplied field value containing the literal string {account_approval_link} is resolved into the real activation URL, including the secret activation key, in the user confirmation email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain the activation link for their own pending registration and activate the account via the ?page=account_activation&key= endpoint, bypassing the manual approval configured on the registration form. Exploitation requires a user-registration form with manual approval enabled and a user confirmation email that includes the {all_fields} merge tag (the default template). Note: On WordPress Multisite installations with site registration enabled, the self-activated account also becomes the Administrator of the subsite created during registration.
affected: wpmudev Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder
ranges: wpmudev Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder

desc: The Translate WordPress with Weglot 2.0 – Multilingual AI Translation plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target site to permit anonymous comment posting (comment_registration disabled) and have at least one Weglot destination language active; on sites with comment moderation enabled, an administrator must approve the carrier and trigger comments before the injected script executes for subsequent visitors.

desc: The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via deserialization of untrusted input that is injected into the Memcached object cache through request Host header key truncation. This allows authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. The additional presence of a POP chain (the bundled Guzzle FileCookieJar, reached through the W3TC\CdnEngine_S3 autoload bridge) allows attackers to write arbitrary files and execute code. This requires the Object Cache to be enabled with the Memcached method backed by the pecl memcache extension and Minify to be enabled; using the same key collision, the attacker first escalates from Subscriber to Administrator.
Exim before 4.100.2 allows attackers to send SMTP traffic that triggers a heap out-of-bounds write in expansion code running as root.

desc: The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires comments to be open, a comment author name containing a literal quotation mark stored via WordPress's ENT_NOQUOTES save pipeline, a raw HTTP client capable of sending unencoded " and > characters in the request path, and — under default WordPress moderation — prior moderator approval of the crafted comment.

product: Simple Calendar – Google Calendar, Events, & ICS Feeds

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the victim to click the attacker-controlled link rendered in the event description, as the javascript: href payload does not fire on page load alone.

desc: The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'extraclasses (also icon, iconcolor, number)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The existing sanitization is ineffective for this context: wp_kses_post preserves bare double quotes (no HTML tags are required in the payload), and wp_json_encode correctly escapes the value for the JavaScript string-literal layer but the reconstituted double quote remains live when Leaflet.ExtraMarkers builds its inner HTML, allowing a single-quoted shortcode attribute value to close the HTML attribute and inject attacker-controlled event handlers.

The Extensions for Leaflet Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'overview-latlng' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by Author-level users because WordPress does not apply kses filtering to post custom fields on save, allowing raw HTML payloads such as event-handler attributes to be stored verbatim and later reflected through the unescaped debug output path.

product: Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce
desc: The Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'start_date' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires the victim — who must hold the manage_woocommerce capability (administrator or shop manager) — to both open the attacker-crafted URL and click the start_date input field on the Export Tools page, as the injected payload is delivered via an onclick handler rather than a page-load event. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
affected: wpcodefactory Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce
ranges: wpcodefactory Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce

product: All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos
desc: The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload must be encoded as C-style escape sequences (e.g. \x3c/\x3e) at storage time so that wp_kses_post — applied on save for users lacking unfiltered_html — passes it through without stripping angle brackets; WordPress core's shortcode_parse_atts() then decodes the escapes into real HTML characters at render time.

desc: The Smaily Connect plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 3.24.0 This is due to the smaily_get_edit_user_id() function reading an attacker-controlled $_GET['user_id'] parameter without performing any ownership or capability check, and then feeding that id into smaily_get_userdata() (which calls get_user_meta()) when rendering the WooCommerce My Account 'edit-account' form via the smaily_print_user_frontend_fields() handler on the woocommerce_edit_account_form action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to read other users' personally identifiable profile data (phone number, date of birth, and gender — including administrators') by appending ?user_id=<target> to the account-details URL.

product: Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO
desc: The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'price_disabled_msg' setting in versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 The uni_cpo_save_settings_data() AJAX handler applies html_entity_decode() to the output of uni_cpo_sanitize_text(), which itself already runs html_entity_decode() before wp_kses(); this double decode allows a double-entity-encoded tag to pass wp_kses as inert text and then be re-materialised as live HTML before being stored in the _cpo_price_disabled_msg post meta and later echoed via do_shortcode() on the single-product page without further escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Shop Manager-level access (edit_products) and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected product page.
affected: moomooagency Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO
ranges: moomooagency Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO

desc: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the `SwpmLevelForm::role()` function applying only `sanitize_text_field()` to the user-supplied `role` parameter with no allowlist, permitting the `administrator` role to be stored verbatim into `swpm_membership_tbl` and subsequently applied to a member's WordPress account via `$user->add_role()` inside `update_wp_user_role()` — also without any role allowlist — when the `swpm_membership_level_changed` action fires. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to create a membership level specifying the `administrator` WordPress role, assign themselves to that level, and thereby elevate their own WordPress account to full Administrator, gaining complete site control including the ability to install plugins, edit themes, and manage users. Exploitation requires that the site owner has lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default `manage_options` capability to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts`, `edit_published_posts`, or `edit_pages`, which grants lower-privileged users access to the SWPM admin dashboard where the vulnerable level-creation form resides. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 The vulnerability exists because the `bulk_operation_menu()` function accepts the `swpm_bulk_change_level_to` parameter from `$_REQUEST` with only `sanitize_text_field()` applied, and passes it to `SwpmMemberUtils::update_membership_level_and_role()` without the `id != 1` allowlist exclusion that every other level-selection path in the plugin enforces — leaving membership level 1, which the installer maps to the WordPress `administrator` role on every fresh install, freely selectable as a bulk-change target. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to elevate their own WordPress account to the full Administrator role, gaining complete site control including plugin installation, user creation, and all other administrator capabilities. Exploitation requires that an administrator has first lowered the plugin's "Admin Dashboard Access Permission" setting from its default of `manage_options` to a lesser capability such as `edit_posts` (Contributor), `edit_published_posts` (Author), or `edit_pages` (Editor), which is a non-default granted-access configuration; the bulk screen's nonce protection (`swpm_bulk_change_level_nonce_action`) does not mitigate the issue because the nonce is emitted on the same page the delegated lower-role user can already reach. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

desc: The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the 'utm_source (and the wp-resetpass-<hash> cookie on the victim side)' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the live password-reset key (rp_key) embedded in the cached reset form, enabling full account takeover of the targeted administrator. Exploitation requires the page-cache engine to be configured as Disk: Basic, Memcached, Redis, or APC with the 'Cache URI with query string variables' option enabled, and the victim must visit an attacker-crafted URL containing utm_source=wp-locations.php while their wp-resetpass cookie remains active.

desc: Webmin through 2.670 before 07d1949 does not escape a save_log.cgi log file path. This is relevant for code execution if a shared-hosting provider offers Webalizer module access.

The Dilemma Lite WordPress plugin through 1.1.1 does not sanitise or escape the choices of dilemmas submitted by visitors before outputting them in the admin dashboard and on the front end, allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators.

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the vlv_value_compare() function in vlv_pagination.c of the Virtual List View module in the **Samba** package. The function uses the sort value from the search result with no check that the result still contains that attribute. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. The LDAP worker that handles the search exits, which disconnects the directory clients that were using that worker, and the directory service starts a replacement worker. Another search of the same kind crashes the worker that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that worker is replaced, so repeating the search keeps the LDAP service from staying available. The same crash follows a search sorted on an attribute the attacker is not allowed to read. The directory removes that attribute from the result, and the comparison uses the missing value.
affected: Samba Samba; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9; Red Hat Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4; Red Hat Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 5

desc: A path traversal (ZIP slip) vulnerability exists in Epiphany when installing WebExtension packages from .xpi files. In src/webextension/ephy-web-extension-manager.c, the decompress_xpi_thread() function extracts XPI archives (ZIP format) to disk using libarchive. For each archive entry, the output path is built by concatenating the intended extraction directory with the raw pathname from the archive: full_path = g_build_filename(path, archive_entry_pathname(entry), NULL); archive_entry_set_pathname(entry, full_path); ret = archive_write_header(ext, entry); The libarchive extraction options did not include ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT or ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS. As a result, archive entries containing parent-directory traversal sequences (for example "../../../../../.bashrc") are written outside the intended web_extensions extraction directory. A malicious .xpi file can therefore overwrite arbitrary files writable by the user running Epiphany, such as ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/autostart/*.desktop, or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. This can lead to persistent code execution on subsequent shell startup or GNOME login. Exploitation requires the victim to install or open a crafted .xpi file. The reporter notes that opening an XPI can trigger extraction even when the WebExtensions feature is not enabled by default. Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.rc. Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2143, which adds ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_NODOTDOT and ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS to archive_write_disk_set_options(). Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2922

A code injection vulnerability exists in Epiphany when the user invokes form autofill from the context menu on a page containing a malicious HTML form. In embed/web-process-extension/resources/js/ephy_autofill.js, getSelector() builds a CSS selector by directly interpolating an element's id attribute: path.unshift(`#${el.id}`); When the user selects an autofill entry, the browser process in embed/ephy-web-view.c previously constructed JavaScript using sprintf with the selector embedded in single quotes: EphyAutofill.fill(PAGE_ID, 'SELECTOR', FILL_CHOICE); Because SELECTOR comes from attacker-controlled page content and is not escaped, a crafted id such as a'); PAYLOAD; var _=(' breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary JavaScript when the script is evaluated. The injected code runs in Epiphany's private autofill script world, which hosts EphyAutofill credential APIs and password manager save/request handlers. The reporter demonstrated a proof of concept that injects credentials into another domain and uses Ephy.permissionsManager to enumerate domains with special permissions. Full exfiltration of all saved passwords was not demonstrated but may be possible given the privileges of this context. Exploitation requires the victim to visit a malicious page, right-click on a form field, and choose an Autofill context menu item. This is a deliberate user action but does not require installing software or entering credentials manually. Affected versions: Epiphany >= 47.beta. Fixed upstream in epiphany 50.6 and 49.9 via merge request !2147, which replaces sprintf-based script evaluation with a WebKit user message and jsc_value_object_invoke_method() passing the selector as a typed string argument. Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/issues/2921

desc: A flaw was found in ModemManager. When parsing a Cell Broadcast Message, some 3GPP data-coding-scheme values (8-bit and reserved character sets) are not handled. The process hits a reachable assertion and aborts. An attacker who can deliver a crafted Cell Broadcast PDU over the radio network, or via a modem AT channel, can cause ModemManager to exit. Repeated aborts can exhaust systemd's default start limit and leave the service failed.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The ASCII-armor reader does not limit the length of a line. Parsing an armored message with a very long line can exhaust memory in the process. Memory use follows the input size, with a small constant factor, and is not a classic amplification.
affected: Red Hat Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10; Red Hat Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9
